page: Amazon Web Services i8ge.metal-24xl is a bare-metal storage-optimized server built on the 64-bit ARM architecture. Powered by AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors running at 2.8 GHz, the non-virtualized host delivers 96 physical cores with single-threaded execution across 96 dedicated vCPUs. The hardware configuration integrates 768 GB of DDR5 system memory, providing 8 GB of RAM per core, along with 36 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 64 KB of L1 data cache per core. Network connectivity reaches a baseline bandwidth of 150 Gbps, with zero GPUs bundled.

The bare-metal configuration includes 60,000 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark measurements indicate exceptional data handling across the memory and storage subsystems, featuring read memory bandwidth of 11,098.12 GB/sec in small cached blocks and uncached sequential bandwidth reaching 481.78 GB/sec for reads and 217.96 GB/sec for writes. The dense local storage array and high DDR5 throughput translate to top-tier transactional metrics, marked by PassMark database operational scores of 48,061.02 and Redis SET throughput exceeding 199 million operations per second.

Compute tests highlight a divergence between single-threaded throughput and parallel execution. Multi-core performance is top-tier, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 26,652 and a stress-ng multi-core metric of 163,762.8. Conversely, single-threaded metrics fall within average industry medians, showing a Geekbench single-core score of 1,906.0. In qualitative terms, cost efficiency is realized through dense resource consolidation: grouping 60 TB of direct-attached NVMe storage, 768 GB of RAM, and 96 physical ARM cores eliminates hypervisor overhead and minimizes cluster footprint for storage-bound architectures.

Given its massive direct-attached NVMe storage capacity, wide memory subsystem, and 150 Gbps network pipe, the i8ge.metal-24xl is best suited for distributed NoSQL systems, large-scale search indexes, transactional relational databases, in-memory key-value caching, and intensive ETL data processing.
description: Amazon Web Services i8ge.metal-24xl is a bare-metal, storage-optimized instance powered by a 96-core AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. Built on the arm64 architecture with one execution thread per physical core, this bare-metal platform integrates 768 GB of DDR5 memory, 60,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a 150 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results reveal exceptional multi-core throughput, top-tier database operations, and Redis performance exceeding 199 million operations per second, contrasting with middle-tier single-core metrics. The hardware configuration lacks dedicated GPUs, focusing strictly on high-density storage and concurrent memory bandwidth. Delivering qualitative infrastructure efficiency via massive bare-metal resource aggregation, this server is engineered for distributed NoSQL databases, transactional engines, in-memory caching clusters, and high-throughput data processing pipelines.
